profile.name: Embedded Amp Model

ai_relevance.text: A small research codebase trains recurrent neural networks to imitate simulated guitar-amplifier nonlinearities and exports the learned model to framework-free C inference.

profile.maturity: Research prototype

novelty.text: First detailed documentation review; this is a baseline, not a claim that the tool launched today.

introduction.text: A small research codebase trains recurrent neural networks to imitate simulated guitar-amplifier nonlinearities and exports the learned model to framework-free C inference.

good_for.text: Exploring the sound-versus-compute tradeoff for a future embedded guitar effect or responsive sound object.

demo.text: Scripts generate local A/B WAVs; no hosted listening demo or completed hardware performance was verified.

installation.text: Follow the documented route for the intended platform; commands below are reference instructions, not tested in this review.
steps: Clone the GitLab source into an isolated Python environment. The reviewed repository root contains no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml; dependencies require manual review.
Use the supplied synthetic target first; no real amplifier recording is required for that demo.
Install a C compiler only if evaluating the C-port comparison. The README does not give a complete cross-platform installation recipe.

usage.text: Exploring the sound-versus-compute tradeoff for a future embedded guitar effect or responsive sound object.
steps: Train the simple synthetic amplifier target and inspect error/model-size output.
Compare the harder target using the generated A/B WAVs.
Validate the C port against PyTorch before planning hardware deployment.

requirements.text: Requirements are drawn from the reviewed documentation; benchmarks are not universal minimums.
requirements.hardware: The reported hidden-size-8 model has 273 parameters and about 1.1 KB weights. A Cortex-M4F load figure is an estimate, not a physical-device benchmark. Training RAM, VRAM, CPU and disk minima are not stated.
requirements.software: Python with PyTorch for training/evaluation; C compiler and libm for exported inference. The README gives no version pins or complete install recipe, and the root has no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.
requirements.platforms: No tested macOS, Windows or Linux matrix is documented. Deployment to a real microcontroller/audio codec remains on the roadmap.

license.text: MIT source. The described demonstrations generate their own synthetic target; real capture recordings and future pretrained distributions would require their own rights review.
license.weights: MIT source. The described demonstrations generate their own synthetic target; real capture recordings and future pretrained distributions would require their own rights review.
license.commercial: The reviewed MIT code license permits commercial activity subject to its conditions. Model weights, data, voices, media assets, services and any required proprietary host need separate permission; unrestricted end-to-end commercial use is not established.
license.cost: Source access has no stated purchase requirement. Hardware, storage and any chosen paid provider or proprietary host can incur costs; no current price quote was verified.

quality.text: Source includes a harder target, model-size/quality comparison and PyTorch-versus-C validation, making the feasibility claim more inspectable than a hardware promise alone. Documentation and source review only; the application was not installed or run.

limitations.text: Both simple and more realistic targets are simulated. Real DI/reamp captures, quantization, knob conditioning and an actual flashed pedal are future work. Developer ESR figures do not independently establish perceptual transparency.

introduction.text: An Electron/FastAPI studio for model-based voice generation, cloning, transcription, dubbing and audiobooks, with multiple selectable engines.

good_for.text: Creating authorized narration and experimenting with timed multilingual dialogue or audiobook chapters.

demo.text: The official site and repository show the cloning, dubbing and model-management workspaces. Language counts are developer claims and depend on the engine.

installation.text: Follow the reviewed project route below; these steps are documentation guidance and were not executed.
steps: Download the open-source Electron release for your platform from the official GitHub release page.
Install its local runtime and select an engine whose model terms fit your project.
Install the required model, then check the reported compute device before generating. Intel Mac users need a remote backend.

usage.text: A small first project that exercises the documented creative workflow.
steps: Use a built-in voice or a clean reference recording you have permission to use.
Generate a short passage, revise pronunciation and timing, then try a longer story or dub.
Review each chapter/segment and export approved audio or video.

requirements.text: Requirements are source-specific. Unreported capacities and untested platforms are not inferred.
requirements.hardware: The site says about 8 GB RAM is enough to start; this is not a guarantee for all engines. The README notes roughly 5 GB free disk for the small CPU PyTorch setup, plus separate model storage. GPU needs vary; the release describes 8 GB GPU audiobook fixes.
requirements.software: Packaged Electron app with managed Python/PyTorch backend and downloaded models. Source development requires Node 22+, Bun, Rust/Cargo and build tools.
requirements.platforms: NVIDIA CUDA on Windows/Linux; Apple Silicon MPS; slower CPU routes. Intel Mac is UI plus remote backend. Windows ARM is experimental and the website/README differ on native packaging, so verify the exact release asset.

license.text: The complete software license was archived and reviewed. Keep software, model weights, dependencies and hosted-service terms separate.
license.weights: AGPL-3.0 application permits commercial use under its terms. The default OmniVoice weights are CC-BY-NC, and its tokenizer has Boson Higgs/Meta Llama terms; paid VoiceStudio code licensing does not replace model permissions. Other engines differ.
license.commercial: The reviewed AGPL-3.0 software license permits commercial use subject to its license, notice and source-sharing obligations where applicable. This does not establish permission for every model, input, output or service.
license.cost: The open-source app has no license fee. Pro/Cloud are separate offerings; model permissions, remote compute and optional translation APIs can add cost.

quality.text: Explicit engine/device reporting and platform documentation help choose a realistic local workflow.

limitations.text: The current release notes describe unsigned/ad-hoc-signed, non-notarized installers and manual Mac updates. Quality and memory vary by engine. Do not equate a local interface with local processing when remote providers are configured. This edition is a documentation review, not an installation or output-quality test.
